divergences: Global NTT dataflow: impl1 fixes iterative Cooley-Tukey decimation-in-time with an internal bit-reversal permutation in the golden; impl2 uses a standard stage/block CT loop — spec pins the butterfly equations but not DIT-vs-DIF or the global ordering.

Crossbar per-stage permutation: impl2 names a stride formula R_s=((2^s)>>3)+1 but does not implement it; impl1 abstracts the crossbar as a flat array entirely — the spec gives no concrete sigma_s, so both abstract it away differently.

Radix-4 fusion details: which two radix-2 stages are fused and the j-rotator sign convention are each derived independently (j=psi^512 chosen to match a standard radix-4 DIT) rather than read from the spec.
FSM / schedule: both reconstruct the stage/block loop and per-stage cycle counts; the spec's 'rearranged twiddle-stationary schedule' is not pinned, so each invents a transition table.
Modular adder/subtractor internal reduction (single conditional ±q vs other) is unspecified; both assume correct mod-q add/sub but neither is told the hardware convention.

missing_fields.item: The paper's actual conflict-free bank-index and offset functions (Sec. III headline result); supplied b(i)=(i+(i>>3))%8 is provably NOT conflict-free for radix-2 strides 64/128/256/512
Crossbar per-stage permutation sigma_s mapping logical operand indices to physical bank/lane ports
Twiddle-ROM address function f(stage s, block index) and negacyclic low/high-half storage layout
Decimation convention (DIT vs DIF) and global butterfly/stage ordering
Radix-4 fusion mapping: which two radix-2 stages fuse into each radix-4 BU, and the j-rotator sign convention
FSM states/transitions and per-stage cycle counts of the rearranged twiddle-stationary schedule
Modular adder/subtractor internal reduction policy (conditional ±q correction count)
Primitive-root generator g (both picked g=11) and full twiddle-factor table contents

property_checks.property: Conflict-free memory mapping for arbitrary radix / arbitrary #BU
property_checks.evidence: Both impls prove the spec's map b(i)=(i+(i>>3))%8 puts both operands in the SAME bank for radix-2 strides >=64; the paper's actual mapping is absent.
Impls produce natural-order output but use an internal bit-reversal in the golden; the HW memory-mapping trick that removes it is not modeled.

property_checks.property: Radix-4: 33% fewer modular multiplications / 20% fewer add-sub
property_checks.evidence: Radix-4 is modeled functionally vs DFT; neither impl counts hardware ops, so the quantified saving is not checked.

property_checks.property: ~50% butterfly hardware saved via symmetric operators
property_checks.evidence: Structural/resource claim; behavioral reproductions cannot exhibit area savings.

property_checks.property: NTT followed by INTT (with N^-1) is identity
property_checks.evidence: Both verify INTT(NTT(x))==x and transform-domain mult == schoolbook negacyclic convolution mod X^N+1.
Both z3-prove correctness exhaustively over x in [0,q^2) with <=2 corrections.

structural_findings: The headline contribution — the conflict-free interleaved-BRAM mapping plus crossbar — is not faithfully reproduced: the supplied bank/offset functions are provably conflict-prone and the crossbar permutation is abstracted to a flat array in both impls.
Twiddle-stationary 'rearranged loop structure' (the source of twiddle reuse) is replaced by a generic Cooley-Tukey stage/block loop in both reproductions.

Radix-4 is realized as a functional 4-point butterfly rather than the symmetric-operator fused datapath the paper uses to claim ~50% hardware and 33%/20% op reductions; the area-time-product advantage is therefore not represented at all.

summary: Reproducibility is high on the datapath math — the spec pins q, psi/omega/N^-1, Barrett mu/k, widths and parallelism so both impls converge on the same negacyclic NTT/INTT, and z3 confirms Barrett and the round-trip identity; the main reproducibility gap is everything structural (the actual conflict-free bank/offset functions, crossbar permutation, twiddle-ROM addressing, DIT/DIF convention and FSM), which each impl reconstructs differently. The biggest fidelity gap is that the paper's defining contribution — the conflict-free memory mapping — is both unspecified and, as supplied, provably non-conflict-free, and the quantified radix-4 op/area savings can't be exhibited by a behavioral model; parameters match the reference almost exactly, but the architecture reproduced is a generic correct NTT rather than CFNTT's scheme.
guessed: Transform flavor -> negacyclic (psi order 2N=2048, omega=psi^2); spec only says 'implied negacyclic', cyclic given as fallback. I implemented negacyclic and verify it against schoolbook mod (X^N+1).

NTT algorithm structure -> iterative Cooley-Tukey decimation-in-time; spec gives only the radix-2/4 butterfly equations, not the global dataflow/ordering. Golden uses an internal bit-reversal permutation even though the HW claims 'no bit-reversal' (that is a memory-mapping trick, not a math difference).
INTT formulation -> inverse NTT with omega^{-1}, scale by N^{-1}=12277, post-twist by psi^{-i}; spec only names the N^-1 unit and 'INTT is identity', not the full inverse pipeline.
Radix-4 output point ordering -> y_m = P(w*j^m) for m=0..3 over points {w, jw, -w, -jw}; derived from the given equations + j=psi^512.
Barrett datapath uses up to 2 conditional subtractions over inputs in [0,q^2); spec gives mu=21843,k=28,max_corrections=2 — verified exhaustively by z3.

Bank conflict-free claim -> the given map b(i)=(i+(i>>3)) mod 8 is a valid STORAGE bijection but does NOT satisfy the asserted conflict-free butterfly property for radix-2 stages s>=6 (where 2^(s-3)≡0 mod 8 makes b(i)==b(i+2^s)). I verify the bijection and the s<6 sub-property, and FLAG the violation rather than asserting a false claim.
PCIe/DMA framing, FIFO handshake, pipeline cycle counts -> treated as non-functional decoration; not modeled in the behavioral verification.

Pipeline cycle counts (mult 3 / add-sub 1 / Barrett 4 / reg 1 = 9) -> taken from spec verbatim but spec itself flags them as 'reproduction defaults pending the paper'; not modeled cycle-accurately, only as functional latency labels
Transform flavor -> negacyclic (psi order 2048) as the spec recommends; cyclic was the rejected fallback
Concrete generator/roots -> g=11, psi=1945, omega=10302, j=psi^512, N^-1=12277 (spec-pinned reproduction values, verified self-consistent mod 12289)
Barrett parameters -> mu=21843, k=28, <=2 conditional corrections (spec-pinned; proven correct exhaustively)
Bank/offset mapping b(i)=(i+(i>>3))%8, o(i)=i>>3 -> implemented as given; it IS a valid storage bijection but is NOT the conflict-free per-cycle map the spec claims (see below)
Radix-4 j-rotator sign convention -> chosen so spec eqs equal the standard radix-4 DIT butterfly (omega4=j=root^(N/4)); verified against direct DFT
FSM transition table & loop arrangement -> modeled as the standard stage/block Cooley-Tukey loop; spec's exact rearranged twiddle-stationary schedule not reproduced
Host PCIe/DMA protocol (128-bit beats, AXI-Stream ready/valid, descriptor framing) -> spec-pinned but purely an I/O boundary, not modeled in the datapath
Crossbar per-stage permutation sigma_s with R_s=((2^s)>>3)+1 -> not implemented; software uses a flat array, so the crossbar is abstracted away
